title: Terminology and OSI
description: The 7 OSI layers, where devices work, and what IP/MAC addresses and switches do.

exercises.prompt: Which list shows the OSI layers in order from Layer 1 to Layer 7?
options: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Physical, Network, Data Link, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
Physical, Data Link, Network, Session, Transport, Presentation, Application
exercises.explanation: Layer 1 Physical, 2 Data Link, 3 Network, 4 Transport, 5 Session, 6 Presentation, 7 Application. (The third option is the right list, but from 7 down to 1.)

options: Data Link
Network
Transport
Session
exercises.explanation: Layer 3 is the Network layer. It handles logical (IP) addressing and routing between networks.

exercises.prompt: What is the layer number of the Transport layer?
exercises.explanation: Transport is Layer 4 (for example TCP and UDP).

exercises.prompt: Match each device to the OSI layer where it mainly works.
exercises.explanation: A hub repeats bits (L1), a switch forwards frames by MAC address (L2), a router forwards packets by IP address (L3).

options: A logical Layer 3 address that identifies a host and is used to route packets between networks
A permanent hardware address burned into a network card
The cable that connects a PC to a switch
A number that identifies an application on a host
exercises.explanation: An IP address is a logical (Layer 3) address. Routers use it to forward packets between networks. The burned-in hardware address is the MAC address.

options: A 32-bit logical address given out by a DHCP server
A 48-bit physical (hardware) address of a network interface, used at Layer 2
The name of a website, such as example.com
A Layer 3 address that routers use to choose a path
exercises.explanation: A MAC address is a 48-bit hardware address (e.g. 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E) used by Layer 2 devices such as switches.

options: Routes packets between different networks using IP addresses
Repeats every incoming signal out of all its ports
Forwards frames only to the port of the destination device, using MAC addresses
Translates domain names into IP addresses
exercises.explanation: A switch learns which MAC address is on which port and forwards each frame only where it needs to go. Routing between networks is a router's job; repeating to all ports is what a hub does.

exercises.prompt: Match each layer number to its name.
exercises.explanation: Layer 5 Session, Layer 6 Presentation, Layer 7 Application.
